narrative.overview: Mensaliza's marketing site should feel like a calm, organized workspace where billing stops being a personal burden. The visual language is humano, organizado, aliviador — direct and empathetic without debt-collector aggression or enterprise fintech coldness. Surfaces are clean and legible; orange is the only brand color; product artifacts do more work than abstract icon grids. WhatsApp is a channel, not a brand color.
keyCharacteristics: Single-accent discipline: Brand orange carries logo, CTAs, focus, accents, and atmosphere. Neutrals stay chroma 0.
Flat tonal layering: Depth comes from borders and muted section bands, not drop shadows.
Artifact-first proof: Hero and feature sections show real product flows.
Mobile-first conversion: Sticky header + bottom demo bar on small screens.
Accessible status: Paid/late/sent states always pair color with text labels.

rules.name: The One-Voice Rule
rules.body: Orange is brand and action. There is no second brand accent. Channel names (WhatsApp, Pix) are copy/icons only — never platform colors.

rules.name: The Tinted-Section Rule
rules.body: On bg-muted sections, never use default muted-foreground at full strength for body copy — darken to ~72% foreground opacity or use ink directly.

rules.name: The Balance Rule
rules.body: Apply text-wrap: balance on h1–h3; text-wrap: pretty on long prose blocks.

rules.name: The No-Shout Rule
rules.body: Display heading max ≤ 3.35rem on this landing. Letter-spacing never tighter than −0.04em.

rules.name: The No Ghost Card Rule
rules.body: Never combine border: 1px solid with a soft wide drop shadow on the same element.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces rest flat. Elevation is semantic (white card on muted band), not decorative.

dos: Do use brand orange for identity, trust accents, automation cues, and conversion CTAs.
Do show concrete product artifacts instead of abstract feature icon grids.
Do keep section radii at rounded-xl (≈12px) and button radii at rounded-lg (8px).
Do pair every status color with a Portuguese text label.
Do maintain ≥4.5:1 body text contrast on tinted bg-muted sections.
Do lead with relief-oriented copy — design should feel aliviador, not cobrança agressiva.
donts: Don't use green of any kind as a brand, accent, atmosphere, or status token — including WhatsApp green. WhatsApp is copy/channel only.
Don't use generic SaaS landing templates: hero metrics, gradient text, cream paper backgrounds, uppercase eyebrow kickers on every section, identical icon-card grids.
Don't adopt aggressive collections or debt-recovery tone — Mensaliza removes embarrassment; it doesn't threaten clients.
Don't position visually as a payment gateway — money goes direct to the professional.
Don't use over-engineered enterprise billing UI patterns that imply complexity, contracts, or maquininha requirements.
Don't use 2026 AI landing tells: editorial serif drop caps, glassmorphism cards, diagonal stripe backgrounds, or insanely rounded 32px+ card radii.
Don't combine border + wide soft shadow on cards (ghost-card pattern).
Don't use side-stripe borders, gradient text, or decorative motion.
Don't use status colors as the only signal — always include text.
